title: Scalar extension of an augmented ring Cech model equals the tensor Cech model
statement: Let (C,J,O) be a small commutative ringed site, A its ring of global sections and T the explicit scalar-extension functor [def-weil-pbc-global-section-scalar-extension]. For a finite global list f let I=(f) in A. Suppose an augmented complex (P,epsilon_P) over A has the ordered Cech model for I [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-cech-data] and P is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Then the tensor extended Cech complex of f [def-weil-pbc-ringed-extended-cech] is isomorphic in D(O) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to T(P), compatibly with its explicit augmentation to O[0]. Derived categories of A-modules and O-module sheaves are assumed, with independent hom universes. This statement contains no functorial ring family, no transition maps, and no Godement construction.

proof.text: Extract K, its augmentation, its ordered localization coordinates and the augmented derived isomorphism from the Cech-model hypothesis. An increasing (q+1)-subset of Fin r cannot exist for q+1>r, so K vanishes above r. It vanishes below zero by hypothesis. Degree zero is free, and every positive term is a finite direct sum of flat localizations. Evaluation at the unique object detects zero objects and flatness on the one-point site. Thus the bounded-above flat criterion proves K is K-flat.

Represent the derived isomorphism K to P by a roof. Equality of its augmented maps in the derived category can be refined by a quasi-isomorphism in the homotopy category; lift that refinement to complexes, making the augmented composites homotopic. Resolve its source by a K-flat W. The two maps W to K and P are quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes, so their global scalar extensions are quasi-isomorphisms. The additive scalar extension preserves the homotopy. Invert the first image and compose with the second image to obtain a derived isomorphism T(K) to T(P) preserving the mapped augmentations. Postcompose with the fixed map T(A[0]) to O[0]. This argument does not identify the two derived-category universes.

Apply the chain-level ordered-to-tensor comparison to the extracted coordinates and augmentation. Apply Q to this chain isomorphism and compose it with the preceding derived isomorphism. Functoriality of Q and the two augmentation equations give the asserted equation.

theorem ringFamilyGlobalExtension_cech
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wA} (RingSiteModules (ringFamilyGlobalRing O))]
    (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → (O.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat).sections)
    (P : CochainComplex (RingSiteModules (ringFamilyGlobalRing O)) ℤ)
    (εP : P ⟶ ringComplexSingle (ringFamilyGlobalRing O))
    (hflat : P.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients)
    (hP : RingComplexHasCechModel (ringFamilyGlobalRing O)
      (ringFamilyGlobalIdeal O r f).val P εP) :
    ∃ e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj (ringedExtendedCech O r f).1 ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj (ringFamilyGlobalExtensionComplex O P),
      e.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (ringFamilyGlobalExtensionAugmentation O εP) =
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (ringedExtendedCech O r f).2
